item.text: I’ve got enough to synthesize the main pattern, but I’m using one final targeted search for any direct 2024 crisis-relief or disaster-response evidence that would qualify as a real positive counterexample.

item.text:
**6B.6**

Bottom line: I found **no strong evidence** that Khamenei personally used crisis data, audits, or corrective feedback loops in 2024 to reduce avoidable suffering. The best positive signals were **tactical de-escalation** and **episodic clemency**. The dominant evidence is negative: a severe water crisis, unresolved environmental and economic shocks, and continued impunity after violent repression.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| *Tehran signals no retaliation against Israel after drones attack* | Reuters | 2024-04-19 | https://www.theprint.in/world/tehran-signals-no-retaliation-against-israel-after-drones-attack/2048236/ | Reuters said Tehran’s no-retaliation posture after the Isfahan incident appeared aimed at averting region-wide war. This is the strongest positive crisis-suffering signal I found, because it likely reduced escalation risk and civilian harm, but it was tactical and short-lived. | 6B.6 |
| *Khamenei approves pardons or commutations for 2,654 inmates* | Xinhua | 2024-06-17 | https://english.news.cn/20240617/61af4b6135bc4f07bd0d76069a67ffe7/c.html | Khamenei approved pardons or commutations for 2,654 inmates, including some security-charge prisoners and foreign nationals. This is limited suffering reduction, but it is discretionary clemency, not a demonstrated crisis-response system. | 6B.6, 6B.3 |
| *Iran’s water crisis leads to alarming ground collapse* | DW | 2024-06-19 | https://amp.dw.com/en/irans-water-crisis-leads-to-alarming-ground-collapse/a-69405927 | DW reported drought and water shortages causing land subsidence, threatening Tehran and hundreds of other towns, affecting at least half of Iranian society. This is direct evidence that a major avoidable crisis was not being effectively contained. | 6B.6, 6B.2 |
| *Iran: Human rights in Iran: Review of 2023/2024* | Amnesty International | 2024-04-24 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/mde13/7972/2024/en/ | Amnesty said authorities failed to address Iran’s environmental crisis, including water shortages and poor water-delivery infrastructure, with especially harsh effects in Khuzestan and Sistan and Baluchestan. This is strong negative evidence on crisis mitigation and on protection of marginalized regions. | 6B.6, 6B.2, 6B.3 |
| *Iran: Two years after Woman, Life, Freedom uprising, impunity for crimes reigns supreme* | Amnesty International | 2024-09-11 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/iran-two-years-after-woman-life-freedom-uprising-impunity-for-crimes-reigns-supreme/ | Amnesty said there were still no effective, impartial investigations into killings, torture, sexual violence, or disappearances, and authorities harassed victims’ families instead. That is strong evidence against transparent, corrective crisis handling. | 6B.6, 6B.3, 6B.5 |
| *Iran rulers seek big turnout as discontent mounts* | Reuters | 2024-03-01 | https://www.theprint.in/world/iran-rulers-seek-big-turnout-as-mounting-discontent/1985060/ | Reuters described sanctions-driven inflation near 40 percent and widespread public belief that the clerical system could not solve the crisis. This is indirect but useful evidence that the regime was not visibly reducing economic-shock suffering. | 6B.6, 6B.2 |

**Search gap**
- I did not find direct 2024 evidence that Khamenei used emergency dashboards, disaster audits, epidemiological data, or public correction loops to reduce suffering.
- I also did not find a clear 2024 case of Khamenei leading a major, documented relief effort for famine, pandemic, or disaster displacement.
- The evidence base is therefore mostly negative, with only weak positives from de-escalation and clemency.
